    - oracle: command
      command: |-
        PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"; D=frontend/dist; A=$D/assets
        [ -d "$A" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: $A absent - build the frontend before grading"; exit 3; }
        [ -f "$D/.vite/manifest.json" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: $D/.vite/manifest.json absent - build.manifest must be enabled so the build itself declares its whole emitted graph"; exit 3; }
        # ROUND 6 / P5-03: the entry document is EXCLUDED from the manifest inventory (it is not a manifest
        # entry), and until now nothing else required it. A build missing index.html therefore passed the
        # completeness check. Require it, and require every /assets/ file it references to resolve on disk.
        [ -f "$D/index.html" ] || { echo "FAIL: $D/index.html is absent - the build produced no entry document, so there is no application to serve however consistent the chunk graph is"; exit 1; }
        IDX=$(node -e '
        const fs=require("fs");const h=fs.readFileSync("frontend/dist/index.html","utf8");
        const u=[...new Set([...h.matchAll(/(?:src|href)="(\/assets\/[^"]+)"/g)].map(m=>m[1]))];
        const miss=u.filter(p=>!fs.existsSync("frontend/dist"+p));
        if(miss.length) console.error("UNRESOLVED: "+miss.slice(0,5).join(" "));
        console.log(u.length+" "+(u.length-miss.length));
        ' 2>/tmp/p100_idx.$$); IRC=$?
        IERR=$(cat /tmp/p100_idx.$$ 2>/dev/null); rm -f /tmp/p100_idx.$$
        [ "$IRC" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the index.html reference walk exited $IRC :: $IDX $IERR"; exit 3; }
        set -- $IDX; IREF=$1; IRES=$2
        case "$IREF" in *[!0-9]*|"") echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the referenced-asset field of the index.html walk returned [$IREF], not a number"; exit 3;; esac
        case "$IRES" in *[!0-9]*|"") echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the resolved-asset field of the index.html walk returned [$IRES], not a number"; exit 3;; esac
        echo "P100-11-ENTRY index_html=present referenced_assets=$IREF resolved_on_disk=$IRES expected referenced>=1 and resolved==referenced"
        [ -n "$IERR" ] && echo "  $IERR"
        [ "$IREF" -ge 1 ] || { echo "FAIL: $D/index.html references no /assets/ file - it is not the entry document of a real build"; exit 1; }
        [ "$IRES" = "$IREF" ] || { echo "FAIL: $IRES of $IREF assets referenced by index.html exist on disk - the entry document points at files this build did not produce"; exit 1; }

        # ── the TWO production counting paths, defined once and used for the fixture and the real tree ──
        # ROUND 4 / C2-08 + P100-C29: count_refs now has count_maps's SHAPE. The traversal is captured into a
        # variable whose status is testable; the previous form fed the loop from a here-document command
        # substitution, which builds a redirection rather than running a command, so it had no reachable $? at
        # all. Three rounds of "add a status check" could not close it because there was nothing to check.
        count_maps() { CM_OUT=$(find "$1" -name '*.map' -type f 2>/dev/null); CM_RC=$?
          [ "$CM_RC" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: find over $1 exited $CM_RC while counting maps"; exit 3; }
          CM=$(printf '%s' "$CM_OUT" | command grep -c . ); [ -n "$CM_OUT" ] || CM=0; }
        count_refs() { CR_OUT=$(find "$1" -name '*.js' -type f 2>/dev/null); CR_RC=$?
          [ "$CR_RC" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: find over $1 exited $CR_RC while enumerating js files for the reference scan - a failed traversal must not read as no matches"; exit 3; }
          CR=0; CR_SEEN=0
          if [ -n "$CR_OUT" ]; then
            OIFS=$IFS; IFS='
        '
            for f in $CR_OUT; do
              IFS=$OIFS
              CR_SEEN=$((CR_SEEN+1))
              command grep -q 'sourceMappingURL' "$f"; g=$?
              case "$g" in 0) CR=$((CR+1));; 1) ;; *) echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: grep exited $g reading $f - a read failure must not normalise to no-match"; exit 3;; esac
              IFS='
        '
            done
            IFS=$OIFS
          fi
          }

        # ── DETECTOR SELF-TEST: the same two functions, on a fixture that must yield exactly 1 each ──
        FX=$(mktemp -d) || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: cannot create a fixture dir"; exit 3; }
        trap 'rm -rf "$FX"' EXIT
        printf '{"version":3}\n' > "$FX/probe.js.map"
        printf 'console.log(1)\n//# sourceMappingURL=probe.js.map\n' > "$FX/probe.js"
        printf 'console.log(2)\n' > "$FX/clean.js"
        count_maps "$FX"; FXM=$CM; count_refs "$FX"; FXR=$CR; FXS=$CR_SEEN
        echo "P100-11-SELFTEST fixture_map_count=$FXM fixture_ref_count=$FXR fixture_js_visited=$FXS expected 1, 1 and 2"
        { [ "$FXM" = "1" ] && [ "$FXR" = "1" ] && [ "$FXS" = "2" ]; } || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the production counting paths scored maps=$FXM refs=$FXR visited=$FXS on a fixture built to yield 1, 1 and 2 - neither counter can be trusted, so no count below means anything"; exit 3; }

        # ── WHOLE-TREE FRESHNESS: every file in dist must postdate the config being graded ──
        OLD=$(find "$D" -type f ! -newer frontend/vite.config.ts 2>/dev/null); FRC=$?
        [ "$FRC" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: find exited $FRC probing whole-tree freshness"; exit 3; }
        NOLD=$(printf '%s' "$OLD" | command grep -c . ); [ -n "$OLD" ] || NOLD=0
        echo "P100-11-FRESH files_not_newer_than_config=$NOLD expected 0 (one build invocation, whole tree)"
        [ "$NOLD" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: $NOLD file(s) under $D predate frontend/vite.config.ts - this tree is not the product of a single build made after the change being graded"; exit 3; }

        # ── COMPLETENESS: the build's own manifest against EVERY file it emitted, both directions.
        # ROUND 4 / C2-09 + P100-C27/C30/C31 + I-02: the walk is recursive over the whole tree and no longer
        # filtered to top-level js/css, so an orphan image or font is visible. A dist file counts as
        # build-emitted unless it is a copy of frontend/public/<same path> (a derived rule, not a file-type
        # guess), a .map, index.html, or the manifest itself. The arbitrary >=400 bound is replaced by the
        # derived exact population recorded in 100-RESEARCH.md §11.1: 473 entries naming 478 files.
        MOUT=$(node -e '
        const fs=require("fs"),path=require("path");
        const m=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("frontend/dist/.vite/manifest.json","utf8"));
        const named=new Set();for(const x of Object.values(m)){if(x.file)named.add(x.file);for(const c of x.css||[])named.add(c);for(const a of x.assets||[])named.add(a)}
        function walk(d,out=[]){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){const f=path.join(d,e.name);e.isDirectory()?walk(f,out):out.push(path.relative("frontend/dist",f))}return out}
        const all=walk("frontend/dist");
        const EXCL=[["*.map","sourcemaps are emitted artifacts but are never manifest entries"],["index.html","the entry document is emitted but not a manifest entry"],[".vite/manifest.json","the manifest cannot name itself"],["same-path copy of frontend/public/","static passthrough, not build output"]];
        const excluded=[];const emitted=[];
        for(const f of all){
          if(f.endsWith(".map")){excluded.push([f,0]);continue}
          if(f==="index.html"){excluded.push([f,1]);continue}
          if(f===".vite/manifest.json"){excluded.push([f,2]);continue}
          if(fs.existsSync("frontend/public/"+f)){excluded.push([f,3]);continue}
          emitted.push(f)}
        const unclassified=excluded.filter(([f,i])=>i===undefined);
        const orphan=emitted.filter(f=>!named.has(f));
        const ghost=[...named].filter(f=>!fs.existsSync("frontend/dist/"+f));
        const byReason=EXCL.map((e,i)=>excluded.filter(([,j])=>j===i).length);
        console.log(Object.keys(m).length+" "+named.size+" "+emitted.length+" "+orphan.length+" "+ghost.length+" "+excluded.length+" "+unclassified.length+" "+byReason.join(":"));
        console.error("EXCLUSIONS "+EXCL.map((e,i)=>e[0]+"="+byReason[i]).join(" ")+"  (each is a NAMED reason; nothing under .vite/ is exempt except the manifest itself)");
        if(orphan.length) console.error("ORPHANS: "+orphan.slice(0,5).join(" "));
        if(ghost.length) console.error("GHOSTS: "+ghost.slice(0,5).join(" "));' 2>/tmp/p100_mwalk.$$); MRC=$?
        MERR=$(cat /tmp/p100_mwalk.$$ 2>/dev/null); rm -f /tmp/p100_mwalk.$$
        [ "$MRC" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the manifest walk exited $MRC :: $MOUT $MERR"; exit 3; }
        set -- $MOUT; ENTRIES=$1; NAMED=$2; EMITTED=$3; ORPHAN=$4; GHOST=$5; EXCLUDED=$6; UNCLASSIFIED=$7; BYREASON=$8
        for fld in "$ENTRIES" "$NAMED" "$EMITTED" "$ORPHAN" "$GHOST" "$EXCLUDED" "$UNCLASSIFIED"; do
          case "$fld" in *[!0-9]*|"") echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: the manifest walk returned a non-numeric field in '$MOUT'"; exit 3;; esac
        done
        echo "P100-11-COMPLETE manifest_entries=$ENTRIES manifest_named=$NAMED build_emitted_on_disk=$EMITTED orphans=$ORPHAN ghosts=$GHOST excluded=$EXCLUDED by_reason=$BYREASON expected 473 478 478 0 0"
        [ "$UNCLASSIFIED" = "0" ] || { echo "INSTRUMENT-CANNOT-RUN: $UNCLASSIFIED dist file(s) were excluded without a named reason - the population must be defined, not assumed"; exit 3; }
        [ -n "$MERR" ] && echo "$MERR" | sed 's/^/  /'
        [ "$ENTRIES" = "473" ] || { echo "FAIL: the manifest declares $ENTRIES entries, not the 473 this app emits (100-RESEARCH.md §11.1) - a freshly built, internally consistent SUBSET of the app has exactly this shape, which is the mutation an entries>=400 floor admitted"; exit 1; }
        [ "$NAMED" = "478" ] || { echo "FAIL: the manifest names $NAMED files, not the derived 478"; exit 1; }
        [ "$EMITTED" = "478" ] || { echo "FAIL: $EMITTED build-emitted files are on disk against 478 named - the emitted set and the declared set are different sizes"; exit 1; }
        { [ "$ORPHAN" = "0" ] && [ "$GHOST" = "0" ]; } || { echo "FAIL: the build's own manifest and the tree it produced disagree - $ORPHAN emitted file(s) are named by no entry and $GHOST named file(s) are missing"; exit 1; }

        # ── ARTIFACT COUNTS: printed as controlled diagnostics; the CHANGED-HUNK criterion is the config oracle ──
        count_maps "$A"; MAP=$CM; count_refs "$A"; REF=$CR; SEEN=$CR_SEEN
        echo "P100-11-DIAGNOSTIC map_files=$MAP sourceMappingURL_refs=$REF js_visited=$SEEN  [NOT GRADED HERE - the graded changed-hunk assertion is the executed config's OFF=false / ON=hidden pair]"
        echo "PASS build completeness"
      text: 'the tree the build vouches for. Both counting functions are self-tested first on a fixture holding one map and two js files of which one carries a reference - they must score exactly 1 and 1, and the reference counter inspects grep''s status PER FILE so a read error exits 3 instead of normalising to no-match, while an empty tree correctly yields 0 rather than the two-line zero the previous version produced. Whole-tree freshness then requires EVERY file under dist to postdate the config, and the build''s own manifest is checked in BOTH directions: no file on disk unnamed, no named file missing. The map and reference counts are PRINTED as diagnostics and are deliberately not predicates - the changed-hunk criterion is the config oracle above.'

<objective>
Close criterion 7. `frontend/vite.config.ts:141` sets `sourcemap: true` unconditionally, so every
production build writes `.map` files carrying populated `sourcesContent`.

The repository already contains most of the fix and does not reach it: the Sentry plugin declares
`filesToDeleteAfterUpload: ['./dist/**/*.map']`, but only inside `isSentryEnabled &&`, so a build
without Sentry credentials generates the maps and deletes nothing.

**The graded changed-hunk assertion is the executed config's returned values**, obtained by loading the
real config twice. The artifact counts are printed as controlled diagnostics and are NOT the gate -
calling a zero "confirmation" does not stop it being an absence. What replaces them as the second gate
is a whole-tree completeness invariant the BUILD ITSELF produces: `build.manifest`.
</objective>

    Two deliberate lines in `build`, and nothing else in the file:

        sourcemap: isSentryEnabled ? 'hidden' : false,
        manifest: true,

    `'hidden'` still emits the maps for the Sentry plugin to upload and delete, but omits the
    `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment so a browser never requests one; `false` on a non-Sentry build emits
    nothing. `isSentryEnabled` is already defined at `vite.config.ts:23`.

    **`manifest: true` is the second line and it is deliberate.** The acceptance needs an invariant that
    binds the WHOLE tree to one build invocation, and the manifest is the only such artifact the build
    itself produces: measured on this app it declares 473 entries naming 478 files, with zero files on disk
    unnamed and zero named files missing. Record that decision and its one cost - an extra
    `dist/.vite/manifest.json` in the bundle output - in the SUMMARY.

    Do not touch `backend/build.mjs` or `agent-runtime/build.mjs` - server bundles no browser receives.
  </action>
